steps.title: Thaw and prepare cells
steps.instruction: Quickly thaw one frozen HEK293T17 aliquot at 37 °C, dilute immediately into pre‑warmed complete medium, and culture for at least one passage until viability exceeds 90 %.

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Transfer the cultured cells to a conical tube, centrifuge at 230 × g for 3 min at room temperature, carefully aspirate supernatant without disturbing the pellet, and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL pre‑warmed (37 °C) complete medium.

steps.title: Count viable cells
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL of the cell suspension with 10 µL Trypan Blue (1:1), count total and viable cells using a Bio‑Rad TC20 or hemocytometer, and confirm viability >90 %.

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension for plating
steps.instruction: Using the viable cell count, dilute cells in complete medium to 2 × 10⁵ cells/mL and prepare 20 mL of this suspension for each nanobody pair; mix gently by inversion or slow pipetting to avoid clumping.

steps.title: Automated cell plating on 384‑well plates
steps.instruction: Load a 12‑channel reservoir (Element 5) with 15 mL of the 2 × 10⁵ cells/mL suspension in the left channel and 5 mL in the right channel; load tip rack (Element 2, tips A‑H12) and two sterile white‑bottom 384‑well plates (Elements 6 and 9, lids removed); verify liquid levels and calibrate Gilson PipetteMax for 20 µL delivery; run the Cell Plating protocol in TRILUTION® micro (13 min 28 s) to dispense 20 µL of cell suspension into each well of both plates.

steps.title: Incubate plated cells overnight
steps.instruction: Replace lids, incubate plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, humidified, for 16–18 h (or until ~70 % confluence). This is a pause point; plates will be used the next day for infection.

steps.title: Prepare 10 µM nanobody solutions
steps.instruction: For each nanobody, calculate the volume of stock needed to make a 10 µM working solution (e.g., 87.5 µL for nanobody 1, 95 µL for nanobody 2) and add at least 10 µL excess; compute medium volume as V₂‑V₁; use the Deep‑Well Plate Map spreadsheet to obtain exact volumes; pipette calculated nanobody and complete medium volumes into separate sterile microcentrifuge tubes, mix gently by pipetting (no vortex).

steps.title: Prepare pseudovirus working solution
steps.instruction: Dilute titrated pseudovirus stock in complete medium to achieve ~1 × 10⁵ RLU per well after the subsequent 2‑fold mixing with nanobodies; determine the required dilution factor (e.g., if an 8‑fold stock dilution gives ~1 × 10⁵ RLU, prepare a 4‑fold working dilution); use the Deep‑Well Plate Map spreadsheet to calculate virus and medium volumes with a 2 mL excess; pipette the calculated volumes into a conical tube.

steps.title: Set up deep‑well plate layout
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, prepare a sterile 96‑well deep‑well plate as follows: add 1,237.5 µL complete medium to H12; 1,155 µL to A11; 825 µL to B–H11 and A–G12; 750 µL diluted pseudovirus to columns 7 and 8 (A–H); 82.5 µL 10 µM nanobody 1 to A11; 6.25 µL complete medium to H10; 6.25 µL 10 µM nanobody 1 to E10 and G10; 6.25 µL 10 µM nanobody 2 to A–H9, A–D10, and F–G10. Ensure the tip is centered and lightly pressed against the well bottom when dispensing 6.25 µL.

steps.title: Run nanobody‑virus mix on Gilson
steps.instruction: Place the prepared deep‑well plate on Element 4 and two sterile 96‑well V‑bottom plates on Elements 6 and 9; load pipette tips (7H and 8‑12A‑H) into Element 2; remove all lids; open the Nanobody‑Virus Mix protocol in TRILUTION® micro and run (33 min 41 s). The program creates two 96‑well V‑bottom plates each containing 50 µL nanobody (or control) plus 50 µL pseudovirus (or control) per well. Verify deck layout before starting.

steps.title: Incubate nanobody‑virus plates
steps.instruction: Incubate the two resulting 96‑well V‑bottom plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 1 h.

steps.title: Transfer mix to cell plates
steps.instruction: Return the 96‑well V‑bottom plates to the same element positions (Elements 6 and 9); place the seeded 384‑well cell plates onto Elements 5 and 8; load full tip boxes into Elements 2 and 3; remove all lids; open the Transfer to Cells protocol in TRILUTION® micro and run (19 min 46 s). The protocol transfers 18 µL of each nanobody‑virus mixture (or control) to each well of the 384‑well plates in quadruplicate.

steps.title: Incubate infection plates
steps.instruction: Return the 384‑well plates to 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ and incubate for at least 56 h (up to 72 h) before luminescence readout. This is a pause point.

steps.title: Prepare Steady‑Glo reagent
steps.instruction: Bring Steady‑Glo liquid substrate (#E254A) to 37 °C, mix the entire content with the powder substrate (#E253A), dispense 10 mL aliquots into tubes, and store at –20 °C overnight.

steps.title: Warm Steady‑Glo on harvest day
steps.instruction: Thaw one 10 mL aliquot per 384‑well plate and bring the prepared Steady‑Glo solution to 37 °C.

steps.title: Distribute Steady‑Glo to cell plates
steps.instruction: Configure the Gilson deck as in the cell‑plating step (12‑channel reservoir in Element 5, 384‑well plates in Elements 6 and 9, tips A‑H12 in Element 2); transfer 15 mL of warmed Steady‑Glo solution into the first and second channels and 5 mL into the third channel of the reservoir; ensure lids are removed; run the Steady‑Glo protocol in TRILUTION® micro (12 min 39 s) to dispense 40 µL into each well.

steps.title: Develop luminescence signal
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at room temperature in the dark for 15 min; wipe condensation from lids, avoid shaking or bumping the plates.

steps.title: Read luminescence and export data
steps.instruction: Measure luminescence with a plate reader (see General note 3), export the raw data in plate format for downstream computational analysis.
